title: Frankenstein, ou le Prométhée moderne
sources: BnF catalogue record cb313619271 <http://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb313619271> || Project Gutenberg #62404, title page transcribed from the Gallica scans <https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/62404> || Gallica scan, tome 1 <https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k1143204> || Romantic Circles, Editions of Frankenstein (bibliography to 1996) <https://romantic-circles.org/Editions/Article/editions-frankenstein>
notes: The first translation of the novel into any language. The title page reads "Par Mme SHELLY, sa nièce": it names the author, misspelled and called Godwin's niece rather than his daughter, three years before any English edition carried her name. It must follow the 1818 text, since the 1831 revision did not yet exist. Scholarship: Anne Rouhette, "Jules Saladin's 1821 Translation of Frankenstein", in Mary Shelley and Europe, ed. A. Braida (Legenda, 2020).

title: Frankenstein oder Der moderne Prometheus
form: novel, with passages cut or altered (VII, 239 p., Fraktur)
sources: K10plus union catalogue PPN 1831430835 (copy at the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach) <https://sru.k10plus.de/opac-de-627?version=1.1&operation=searchRetrieve&query=pica.ppn%3D1831430835&recordSchema=marcxml> || Bodammer, "Translating Disability: The First German Translation of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein" (2025) <https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/publications/translating-disability-the-first-german-translation-of-mary-shell/> || Projekt Gutenberg-DE transcription (from a 2009 Fischer Taschenbuch reprint) <https://projekt-gutenberg.org/authors/mary-shelley/books/frankenstein-oder-der-moderne-prometheus> || Romantic Circles, Editions of Frankenstein (bibliography to 1996) <https://romantic-circles.org/Editions/Article/editions-frankenstein>
notes: Title conflict: Romantic Circles gives "der neue Prometheus"; the catalogue record of the physical copy reads "Der moderne Prometheus". Some e-text reprints claim a first appearance in 1908; no 1908 record was found in DNB or K10plus, so 1912 stands. Widtmann followed the 1831 text: his first chapter has Elizabeth adopted from a peasant family near Lake Como, a story Shelley added in 1831 (checked in the Gutenberg-DE transcription). Bodammer argues he cut and altered the creature's education and inner life. Altmann was a publisher of occult titles. No facsimile scan found; the passage here comes from a 2009 reprint, not checked against the 1912 printing.

sources: NDL Digital Collections, 國のもとゐ 1(3), June 1889: 新造物者 (第一篇) <https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1599950> || NDL Digital, 1(4), July 1889: 新造物者 (第二編) / 瓠廼舍主人 <https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1599951> || NDL Digital, 1(5), August 1889: 新造物者 (第三篇) <https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1599952> || KAKEN project 22K00490 (Nakagawa): the 1889-90 serial, its base text and translator <https://kaken.nii.ac.jp/grant/KAKENHI-PROJECT-22K00490> || NDL record of the first Japanese book translation, 巨人の復讐 (1948) <https://ndlsearch.ndl.go.jp/books/R100000002-I000000840775>

The scans are public domain but exist only as page images, so no passage is included here.

title: Frankenstein
publisher: Donatello De Luigi (series "Il romanzo nero", no. 1)
sources: Letizia Carbutto, "La fortuna di Mary Shelley in Francia e in Italia: dal Frankenstein di Jules Saladin (1821) a quello di Ranieri Cochetti (1944)", de genere <https://www.degenere-journal.it/index.php/degenere/article/view/269> || Alessandra Zangrandi, "La prima traduzione italiana di Frankenstein" (2022) <https://iris.univr.it/handle/11562/1085598> || Romantic Circles, Editions of Frankenstein (bibliography to 1996) <https://romantic-circles.org/Editions/Article/editions-frankenstein>
notes: Published 10 May 1944 in Rome. Carbutto shows from the text that Cochetti followed the 1818 edition; he dropped the subtitle, the dedication, the epigraph and the prefaces, cut quotations such as "Mutability" and "Tintern Abbey", and changed the three-volume structure. The next Italian translation was B. Tasso's (Rizzoli, 1952). Not checked against the SBN catalogue.

title: Frankenstein: o criador e o monstro
sources: Lilian Agg Garcia, "Mary Shelley e as cartas de Frankenstein" (PhD thesis, UFSC), read only in search snippets <https://repositorio.ufsc.br/handle/123456789/186557> || Romantic Circles, Editions of Frankenstein (bibliography to 1996) <https://romantic-circles.org/Editions/Article/editions-frankenstein> || Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal, "Frankenstein: 200 anos" exhibition <https://bnportugal.gov.pt/index.php?Itemid=1326&catid=169%3A2018&id=1315%3Adestaque-frankenstein-200-anos-jan-8-fev&lang=pt&option=com_content&view=article>
notes: Brazil came first. One source (the Garcia thesis) gives this 1943 edition, whose only known copy, in the Biblioteca Nacional in Rio, is incomplete; Rio as the place is inferred from the publisher's seat. The subtitle may point to a popular or film-influenced version. The next Brazilian translation is Caio Jardim's (São Paulo, 1957). In Portugal the earliest found is Márion Martins Carvalho's (Lisbon: Estampa, 1972), unverified: the Portuguese union catalogue blocked our queries.
